title: A journey through Prehistory and the Ancient Age
summary: Review life in the past, from prehistoric caves to large Roman cities.
keyIdeas: Prehistory is divided into the Palaeolithic, the Neolithic and the Metal Ages.
The invention of writing marks the end of Prehistory and the beginning of the Ancient Age.
The Romans changed the landscape by building roads, aqueducts and carefully planned cities.

basicKnowledge: C. Sociedades y territorios › Sociedades en el tiempo

activities.prompt: Which major development marks the end of Prehistory and the beginning of the Ancient Age? 📜
activities.explanation: Writing allowed people to leave written records of events. This is why it marks the beginning of recorded history.
activities.hint: It made it possible to record information using symbols and letters.

activities.prompt: In the Palaeolithic, people were nomadic: they moved from place to place to find food by hunting and gathering.
activities.explanation: Palaeolithic groups moved to find food when local resources became scarce, rather than living in permanent villages.

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence about the great change in the Neolithic.
activities.explanation: Many Neolithic communities built permanent villages as they began farming and keeping animals. A settled way of life means living in one place.
activities.sentence: As people learnt to grow plants and keep animals, their way of life became ___.

activities.prompt: Match each development to the period in which it appeared.
activities.explanation: New skills and inventions in each period changed how people lived.

activities.prompt: Sort these archaeological remains by their historical period.
activities.explanation: Where remains come from and their age help us distinguish prehistoric remains from Roman ones. A Roman object belongs to recorded history even if it has no writing on it.

items.text: A cave painting of bison at Altamira
A bronze axe from a prehistoric village
A Roman theatre with stone seating

activities.prompt: Put these historical periods in order, from earliest to latest.
activities.explanation: Prehistory includes the Palaeolithic, the Neolithic and the Metal Ages. The Ancient Age came afterwards.

activities.prompt: Read the text carefully and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: Roman engineering and town planning improved travel and cleanliness in cities.
activities.title: A visit to a Roman city
activities.text: Lucía's class visits the ruins of Segóbriga, an ancient Roman city. An archaeologist shows them the large stone theatre, where women and men watched comedies. Next, they walk along a Roman road paved with huge stone slabs. These helped carts travel without getting stuck in mud. Near the city walls, they see the remains of an aqueduct. It carried clean water from a spring to the city's fountains. The Romans used water to help keep their cities clean and healthy.

questions.prompt: What was the Roman city's aqueduct used for?
questions.explanation: The aqueduct carried water from a spring to the city.
options: Defending the city walls against enemies

questions.prompt: What was the advantage of the Roman road's stone slabs?
questions.explanation: The hard slabs made a firm surface that carts could travel along easily.
options: They stopped wheels getting stuck in mud
They kept the road warm all winter

activities.prompt: We now know that women and men cooperated in Prehistory. Which activities did they share?
activities.explanation: The whole group helped people survive. Women and men shared tasks such as finding food and protecting the group.
activities.hint: Think about finding food in nature.
options: Hunting small animals and gathering plants

activities.prompt: Adrián visits Mérida and crosses a Roman bridge that pedestrians still use. What does this show?
activities.explanation: Roman stone structures were so well designed that many are still used two thousand years later.
options: The excellent quality and strength of Roman engineering
Roman bridges were built last year
People in the Ancient Age used materials that did not last long

activities.prompt: Someone wants to touch a painting in a prehistoric cave. What should Nerea remind them to do? 🎨
activities.explanation: Touching paintings can damage them. We must follow the rules about access, lighting and photographs.
options: You can touch it if you wash your hands first
Look without touching and follow the visiting rules
You can use any camera flash, even if it is forbidden
